Hi Tessa / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we’re ready to move forward with Dedicated capacity for our document ingestion and on-demand Q&A flows. Before we lock calendar times for provisioning, wanted to capture the operational constraints from our side so the turn-up goes smoothly: 

- Primary regions: us-west-2 preferred, fallback us-east-1 for DR.
- Target steady-state qps (inference requests): 120 req/s, 95th token latency target ~250ms.
- Workload pattern: weekday business-hours spike (09:00–18:00 PDT), nightly batch jobs from 01:00–03:30 PDT that run heavy embeddings.
- Data residency: all payloads stay in our VPC; keys managed by our KMS.

Can you share a short checklist for the provisioning handoff (network, IAM, test traffic plan, canary window) and the recommended autoscaling/burst policy? We also need a rough ETA for warm pool sizing and whether Redwood supports short-term bursts beyond reserved capacity for launches.

Attaching a network diagram and our initial capacity estimate (high-level).

Hi Andrew — great to see these constraints up front, that helps a lot. Below is a concise operational handoff checklist and our recommended guardrails for a safe first cutover. I included owner assignments so we can lock calendar slots.

Operational handoff checklist (what Redwood will validate and what we need from StellarDocs):
- Network & routing: confirm VPC peering / Transit Gateway CIDRs, open outbound on required ports, and provide NAT config example. Owner: Monica.
- IAM & access: Service account + least-privilege role for provisioning + KMS key ARN for envelope encryption. Owner: Rishi.
- SOW & billing attachments: counter-signed SOW draft (see attached redwood_sow_v1.docx). Owner: Tessa (ops), cc procurement.
- Test traffic plan: we recommend a 72-hour canary with stepped qps: 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%. Define synthetic prompts and performance gates (P1: token latency 95th < 350ms). Owner: Marissa.
- Warm pools & burst: suggest baseline min_nodes=2; target steady nodes=6; max_nodes=12. Burst policy: allow temporary burst to +4 nodes beyond reserved for up to 4 hours for launches (subject to capacity). We’ll coordinate pre-warm for the launch day. Owner: Monica / infra.
- Autoscale policy: CPU / GPU utilization + queue-length thresholds; default: scale-up when GPU util >70% for 60s or queue >50 reqs for 30s; scale-down when util <40% for 300s. Owner: Rishi.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for repeated user contexts; we’ll pre-warm most common prefixes during the canary. Owner: Marissa.
- Monitoring & alerts: create dashboards for 95th latency, token throughput, error-rate; on-call escalation path to Redwood SRE + StellarDocs infra. Owner: Tessa.

Tentative timeline (subject to SOW signature):
- 09/04–09/06: Network & IAM exchanges, SOW countersign (procurement).
- 09/07: Provision baseline pool (min 2 nodes) in us-west-2; smoke tests.
- 09/08–09/10: 72-hour canary with stepped qps (5/25/50/100%).
- 09/11: Review metrics + sign-off for go-live + schedule pre-warm for launch.

Attachments: redwood_sow_v1.docx (SOW draft).

Let us know any hard constraints (e.g., no maintenance window on your side 09/08) and I’ll update the timeline.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0112

Andrew — answering both points and adding the implementation run cadence below.

RTO & rollback: Our standard canary rollback RTO is 30 minutes for traffic cutover (we cut traffic back to hosted endpoints or previous model variant). Full cluster decommissioning rollback can take up to 2 hours depending on reclaiming volumes.

Burst billing model: Reserved capacity billed per monthly committed nodes. Bursts are billed at an on-demand uplift rate; we can set a daily burst-spend cap in the billing profile and configure alerts when predicted spend exceeds 80% of that cap. I attached the sample estimates you requested (capacity_estimates.xlsx).

Implementation run cadence & owners (detailed):
- Pre-provision (ASAP): Exchange VPC CIDRs + KMS ARN + test subnet (Owner: Rishi).
- Provision baseline (09/07): Redwood will provision min_nodes=2, baseline networking checks, and run smoke tests with synthetic prompts (Owner: Monica).
- Canary (09/08—09/10): Stepped qps with performance gates; daily sync at 09:30 PDT to review metrics and tweak scale thresholds (Owner: Marissa).
- Pre-warm & launch (post-signoff): Schedule a 2-hour pre-warm window on launch date; Redwood will hold +3 warm nodes for the window (Owner: Monica & Tessa).
- Post-launch (30 days): Weekly quality checks and one monthly capacity review to right-size nodes / quantization profiles (Owner: Rishi).

Escalation contacts: Redwood SRE (pager + email) and Monica for urgent network issues; Tessa for SOW/billing and Marissa for performance tuning.

Next steps for us:
1. Rishi: send required IAM role template + KMS ARN field by EOD 09/08.
2. Andrew/procurement: countersign SOW and confirm daily burst-spend cap.
3. Marissa: upload synthetic test plans to the shared Drive folder and add the test prompts (link below).

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood-Stellar-Handbook
